description:
Wide Horizons (BETA)

Dependencies: LunaLib, GraphicsLib and Particle Engine

Description

Important: v1.4.x is Not Save-Compatible with older version 1.3.x

Wide Horizons lets you expand the Starsector galaxy by up to 300%.
With in-game setting, the entire universe scales up: sector size, star systems, ruins, Remnants, gates, and more.
Major factions are redistributed across this vast space in a lore-consistent way, offering a fresh sense of exploration and strategic depth.

Key Features:
Bigger Galaxy (scalable): Expand the sector up to 125-300% and tweak density right from the Settings.
Realistic systems: Efforts are made to generate systems that are as realistic as possible.
Spoiler
Wide Horizons’ “Realistic Systems” option changes how newly generated, uninhabited star systems are built.

Instead of placing planets in a more random vanilla-style way, the mod tries to create systems that feel more believable and physically structured. It takes things like the star type, luminosity, habitable zone, snow line, system age, and orbital spacing into account.

In practice, this means:

hotter inner planets are more likely to be barren, irradiated, rocky, or volcanic
colder outer planets are more likely to be icy or frozen
habitable worlds are more likely to appear near the star’s habitable zone
gas giants usually form farther out, often beyond the snow line
asteroid belts, dust rings, ice rings, moons, and stable points are placed in more sensible locations
older or younger systems can have different structures, such as more debris, belts, or less stable planet layouts

The feature is meant to make exploration feel more natural and varied, while still staying close to Starsector’s vanilla style.

It does not rebuild important hand-made vanilla systems, core worlds, market systems, or most mod-added systems. It mainly affects random, unexplored procgen systems.
Fuel scaling: This allows you to better adjust your fuel consumption if you find it too difficult to reach remote locations.
Supply scaling: This allows you to better adjust your supply compensation if you find it too difficult to reach remote locations.
Mission timer adjustment: This scales the mission timer based on the size of the galaxy, giving you more time to reach distant locations.
Strange Hyperspace: regions that change storms, visibility, and travel.
Discovery Gameplay: Some systems start hidden; uncover them over time, earn small XP, and get clear messages. Can be turned on & off.
Hyperspace Music: The custom Wide Horizons hyperspace music can be turned on or off at any time.
Performance Mode: Generates a smaller, more performance-friendly sector while automatically adjusting its content to match the reduced size.
More Variety, Vanilla-friendly: More ruins, remnants, salvage and points of interest kept close to the vanilla feel.
Huge Mod Support: Fixed placement for 60+ popular mods so their systems land in sensible spots.
Dark Star Content (WIP): Void & Pulse stars with unique hazards, pulses, and probes to find.
Storyline (WIP): Follow the new storyline surrounding the AI faction "EidolON".
Custom Start (WIP): "Black Project" start with a brief introduction and a survival-focused opening with a continuing story.

Wide Horizons now offers full support with Customizable Star Systems!
Our internal helper reads all entries from customStarSystems.json using CSS’s own merge logic, and registers those systems for proper positioning and scaling in the expanded Wide Horizons sector.
CSS systems are matched by:
explicit "name" (first star) or matching "setLocation" coordinates
Systems without a name and without coordinates cannot be matched.
Please include one or both in your system definitions to enable Wide Horizons support.

Installation
Download and extract into your Starsector/mods/ directory.
Enable "Wide Horizons" in the launcher.
Start a new game (preferably with Nexerelin).
Enjoy your vastly expanded universe!

Version 1.3.0 (October 2025)

Eidolon Update
New, unexplained phenomena can occur in certain systems.
Strange fleets may appear with unfamiliar behavior.
Battles against them feel different from anything else in the Sector.
Aftermath of these encounters will not be what you expect.
Unique atmosphere and music included.
Be prepared… or don’t. You’ll find out when it happens.

Core recognition update
Improved detection of „Core Worlds“ (no settings changed):
Vanilla core worlds stay the same.
Modded capital systems are now auto-recognized via tags or inhabited markets.
Mod authors can explicitly register their capitals as „core“ via the new API.
Result: Core worlds keep using the dedicated core scaling (as before), but this now reliably applies to modded cores as well.
Note: It's not final yet, there may still be mistakes.

AI behavior adjusted
The AI now responds correctly to changes made in the wide horizon.
This applies to Abyss, Deep Hyperspace storms, and Strange Hyperspace.

Hyperspace visuals & mod compatibility
Fixed double-drawn hyperspace (compatibility with mods like Erexeus Tech Complex):
Wide Horizons now recognizes when another mod adds its own small, PNG-based hyperspace patch (e.g., around horizonVortex)
and lets that render as intended without repainting the whole hyperspace a second time.
Result: no overlaid or mirrored second layer; ETC’s spiral mask shows correctly.

System-safe behavior:
Hyperspace terrain that lives inside star systems now uses the mod’s tiles exactly as provided (no Wide Horizons extras), preventing unintended visuals in local/system scenes.
Single main hyperspace layer: Internally, the game now picks exactly one “main” hyperspace layer for Wide Horizons to generate the big cloud backdrop;
all other hyperspace terrains from mods act as overlays only.

Reliability & polish
Safer startup order: Wide Horizons initializes its hyperspace once, avoids conflicting re-initializations, and cooperates with mods that place their own effects.
Cleaner logs: Startup messages are clearer; one main hyperspace init is reported, and small overlays identify themselves as such.

Dark Star systems
Content unchanged; planets and moons still use the lore name pool.
Only the internal IDs changed to match vanilla for maximum stability.

Salvage & points of interest
Derelicts/wrecks now use fully unique IDs per system, preventing edge cases with salvage, intel, and scanning.

Stability & compatibility
Added a smart Bypass Window so older mods (like ASS) can place content first fewer worldgen crashes.
Fixed a crash when using Wide Horizons together with What We Left Behind and ArthrsShipsNShit (ASS).
Clearer error messages now point to the exact mod if something still fails.
Removed legacy internal “dedupe/ID utility” code; system placement logic made idempotent to avoid repeat registrations.
Overall compatibility with other sector-expanding mods is improved.

Worldgen Tweaks
More balanced spread of Derelicts, Ruins, Remnants, Misc.
Cryosleepers and inactive gates placed more sensibly.
Remnant beacons space out better on larger sectors.

Hotfix: Slipstreams
Fixed an issue where some slipstreams stayed permanent or static, especially near the Abyss.
The game now correctly resets and cycles slipstreams as intended.
Existing “frozen” streams will start moving again after a few in-game weeks.

Hotfix: Dark Star & Colony List
Fixed a rare issue where a newly founded colony could fail to appear in the colony overview.
Cause: duplicate hidden planet tokens from internal ID conflicts.
Fix: all planets and moons now use the vanilla auto-ID system, eliminating duplicates and improving mod compatibility.

Hotfix: Discovery Mode
Fixed crash when using features that open dialogs during hyperspace (e.g., Industrial Evolution’s fleet detachment) while Discovery Mode was enabled.
Discovery Mode is now UI-only: hidden systems are only hidden on the map for the player.
The AI and other mods can still see and interact with all systems normally.
No more weird log spam from legacy dialog hooks. Removed the old workaround that could cause warnings.
Smoother reveals: systems reliably reappear on the map once you discover or enter them.

Hotfix: Theme Generator Compatibility
Fixed: An issue where HMI systems “Seele” and “Mansa” could fail to appear in new games.
Our theme generation now correctly integrates mod-registered generators (e.g., HMIThemeGenerator) into Wide Horizons’ pipeline.
Compatibility: Improved support for mods that add content via theme-based system generation. This reduces the chance of missing themed systems in the outer sector.
Stability: No balance changes; this is a generation-phase fix only.
Note: You’ll need to start a new game to see the effect, since sector generation happens at game start.

Hotfix: Abyss Seam
Improved how the game samples and covers map tiles at the Abyss boundary to remove tiny gaps.

Hotfix:
Fixed an issue where only a very small number of warning beacons were generated in hyperspace.
Beacon generation now correctly scales with sector size and matches vanilla behavior more closely.
Players will encounter the expected variety of low, medium, and high-level warning beacons across the sector.

Special thanks to all reporters and bugatti_echelon for reporting and helping track down the issue!

Description

Important: v1.4.x is Not Save-Compatible with older version 1.3.x

Wide Horizons lets you expand the Starsector galaxy by up to 300%. 
With in-game setting, the entire universe scales up: sector size, star systems, ruins, Remnants, gates, and more. 
Major factions are redistributed across this vast space in a lore-consistent way, offering a fresh sense of exploration and strategic depth.

Key Features:
Bigger Galaxy (scalable): Expand the sector up to 125-300% and tweak density right from the Settings.
Realistic systems: Efforts are made to generate systems that are as realistic as possible.
SpoilerWide Horizons’ “Realistic Systems” option changes how newly generated, uninhabited star systems are built.

Instead of placing planets in a more random vanilla-style way, the mod tries to create systems that feel more believable and physically structured. It takes things like the star type, luminosity, habitable zone, snow line, system age, and orbital spacing into account.

In practice, this means:

hotter inner planets are more likely to be barren, irradiated, rocky, or volcanic
colder outer planets are more likely to be icy or frozen
habitable worlds are more likely to appear near the star’s habitable zone
gas giants usually form farther out, often beyond the snow line
asteroid belts, dust rings, ice rings, moons, and stable points are placed in more sensible locations
older or younger systems can have different structures, such as more debris, belts, or less stable planet layouts

The feature is meant to make exploration feel more natural and varied, while still staying close to Starsector’s vanilla style.

It does not rebuild important hand-made vanilla systems, core worlds, market systems, or most mod-added systems. It mainly affects random, unexplored procgen systems.
Fuel scaling: This allows you to better adjust your fuel consumption if you find it too difficult to reach remote locations.
Supply scaling: This allows you to better adjust your supply compensation if you find it too difficult to reach remote locations.
Mission timer adjustment: This scales the mission timer based on the size of the galaxy, giving you more time to reach distant locations.
Strange Hyperspace: regions that change storms, visibility, and travel.
Discovery Gameplay: Some systems start hidden; uncover them over time, earn small XP, and get clear messages. Can be turned on & off.
Hyperspace Music: The custom Wide Horizons hyperspace music can be turned on or off at any time.
Performance Mode: Generates a smaller, more performance-friendly sector while automatically adjusting its content to match the reduced size.
More Variety, Vanilla-friendly: More ruins, remnants, salvage and points of interest kept close to the vanilla feel.
Huge Mod Support: Fixed placement for 60+ popular mods so their systems land in sensible spots.
Dark Star Content (WIP): Void & Pulse stars with unique hazards, pulses, and probes to find.
Storyline (WIP): Follow the new storyline surrounding the AI faction "EidolON".
Custom Start (WIP): "Black Project" start with a brief introduction and a survival-focused opening with a continuing story.

Wide Horizons now offers full support with Customizable Star Systems!
Our internal helper reads all entries from customStarSystems.json using CSS’s own merge logic, and registers those systems for proper positioning and scaling in the expanded Wide Horizons sector.
CSS systems are matched by:
explicit "name" (first star) or matching "setLocation" coordinates
Systems without a name and without coordinates cannot be matched.
Please include one or both in your system definitions to enable Wide Horizons support.

Prevents Broken Starts:
    This prevents issues with overlapping or misplaced systems and ensures a smoother gameplay experience.

        The core region remains rich with spiral nebula patterns.

Fixed:

    Several HMI star systems (Opuntia, Kamikaze, Mercy, Obsidian) were not appearing at the correct locations in the sector map.
    Their positions now match the intended layout, just like in vanilla and other supported mods.

Version 1.0.6 (July 2025)

Core System Architecture Rework:

Foundation Rebuilt for Large-Scale Sector Support
    The internal structure for star system placement, registration, and alignment has been completely reworked.
    WideHorizons now uses a centralized framework to accurately reposition systems—Vanilla and modded—alongside their content, terrain, and static entities.

Content-Aware Positioning
    Systems are no longer just moved by coordinates: all attached entities (e.g., planets, stations, derelicts) are repositioned intelligently as part of the system structure.
    This ensures thematic consistency and visual accuracy across the entire sector.

Integrated Hyperspace Coordination
    Hyperspace terrain is now automatically adjusted around repositioned systems.
    Clearing logic respects final system locations and is synchronized with terrain generation, preventing fog collisions or obscured entrances in large sectors.

Fixed Position System Framework
    A new utility layer handles persistent placement of star systems across game sessions.
    Mod systems are only repositioned if they exist and are detected, ensuring safe and dynamic support for a wide range of external content.

Version Checker Integration
    WideHorizons now supports the Version Checker.
    You’ll be notified in the main menu whenever a new version of WideHorizons is available—no more guessing or missing important updates.

Fixed:
    Some systems (e.g. Mayasura) had misaligned stations, gates, or relays after being moved in the larger sector.
    This was caused by entities using fixed setLocation(...) coordinates without orbits, which did not follow the moved system center.
    Solution: All non-orbital system entities (e.g. gates, beacons, custom stations) are now automatically attached to their system’s star and follow correctly when the system is repositioned.
    Also excluded dynamic entities (like scanners, spawners or patrol anchors) from being locked to system centers, preserving intended behaviors.

Bugfixes and Improvements:
– Fixed crash caused by mismatched tile string length
– Prevented abyss regions from being overwritten during refill
– Added tile length validation for safe terrain initialization
– Reduced duplicate clearing calls for better performance
– Added terrain auto-initialization fallback

Hyperspace Terrain Clearing and Refilling:
    Now the mod properly clears hyperspace nebula (“fog”) only around registered star systems and safely refills those areas on load. This prevents unwanted fog edits and improves navigation and visibility in a larger sector.

System Repositioning Stability:
    Star systems and their static entities are now consistently registered and repositioned based on saved coordinates, ensuring stable layouts after loading or sector generation. All non-orbital entities are auto-attached to the system’s star.

Developer Mode Logging:
    All internal logs are now gated behind Developer Mode. You’ll only see detailed debug output if DevMode is active, keeping the log clean during normal gameplay.

Central Logging via WHDevLogger:
    A new WHDevLogger utility handles all info, warn, and error output. It ensures consistent formatting, centralized control, and dev-mode-only output where appropriate.

Bugfixes and Internal Improvements:
– Fixed duplicate position updates caused by redundant system re-registration
– Ensured proper initialization of hyperspace terrain during generation and load
– Improved handling of abyss tiles to prevent invalid terrain overwrite
– Logging now includes tile debug info (before/after) for clear diagnostics
– Automatically skips auto-fix of dynamic entities to preserve AI and script behavior

What This Means for Players
– Clearer and more immersive hyperspace visuals around key systems
– Stable and reliable sector layout during both new game and reload
– Minimal log clutter unless actively debugging
– Improved performance and compatibility with terrain-related mods

Accurate System ID Matching
    System detection is now based on the actual Starsector-internal IDs, ensuring precise registration regardless of name capitalization or localization.
    Mods using duplicate system names (e.g., “Acheron”) are handled cautiously to avoid conflicts.

Duplicate System Protection
    Systems with identical IDs from multiple mods (like SCY and DPL) are safely checked before repositioning.
    Only one version is moved - whichever was actually created - preventing layout bugs or invisible systems.

Mod Detection-Based Placement
    Fixed system positioning is now fully conditional: systems are only repositioned if the corresponding mod is detected.
    This avoids errors and maintains a clean layout for each user’s mod setup.
